mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above its 12-month moving average signals an active monetary tightening cycle that elevates discount rates for equity valuation, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0% indicates labor market deterioration that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals broad-based economic contraction in manufacturing and residential sectors, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: doc:Industrial Production and Housing Market Interdependence
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both INDPRO and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising), a decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the last month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS declines during FEDFUNDS rising periods, or the Rank IC for RSAFS in tightening cycles is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and fall in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals severe labor market deterioration that weakens consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: doc:Labor Market Deterioration and Consumer Spending
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 quarterly growth > 3.0%), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals an overheated housing market that triggers reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: doc:Late-Cycle Housing Market and Equity Valuation
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST declines during GDPC1 growth > 3.0% periods, or the Rank IC for HOUST in late-cycle expansions is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals accelerating inflation that prompts immediate equity market sell-offs due to anticipated monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over any 1-year rolling window is below 0.03.
